explain: Aligning the road at ground level is the most economical as it minimizes earthwork costs (cutting and filling) and drainage issues.

q: 8. In full grouted method of construction of Bituminous roads, Bitumen is applied at the rate of .............
explain: Full grout involves heavy application of binder to penetrate the full depth of the course, typically 8 to 14 kg per square meter.

q: 9. In full grouted method of construction of Bituminous roads, the second coat of Bitumen is applied at the rate of .............
explain: Following the primary grout, a second application (seal or finish) is applied at a lower but still substantial rate of 4-8 kg/m².

q: 10. In full grouted method of construction of Bituminous roads, rolling is done with .............
explain: A lighter roller (8-ton) is used for initial compaction to avoid crushing stones, followed by a heavier (10-ton) roller for final density.

q: 11. In semi-grouted Macadam Pavement the hoggin material is .............
explain: Fine sand is often used as a 'hoggin' or filler material in the lower portions of semi-grouted macadam to reduce the required bitumen.

q: 12. In the premix method of Bitumen road construction aggregate is also heated .............
options: to economics the quantity of Bitumen
explain: Heating aggregates ensures they are dry and at a similar temperature to the bitumen, which maintains workability and prevents the binder from cooling too fast.

q: 13. The wall constructed for the stability of a filling portion of a road on the downhill side, is known as
explain: Retaining walls are built on the downhill side (valley side) to support the road embankment filling.

q: 14. Stability of hill slopes depends upon
explain: Stability is determined by the internal friction of the soil (nature), the steepness (angle), and the presence of rock bedding planes (geology).
